cultural.vision_reason: The photo shows two women with elaborately styled hair (one with long twisted/plaited extensions reaching to the waist, coated in ochre paste typical of Himba/Herero hairstyling), traditional skirts, and metal arm/leg bangles, standing against an earthen wall — a documentary photograph of dress and hairstyling practice consistent with Himba/Herero culture in Namibia.

Portrait of a young Himba woman wearing traditional beaded headdress, chin ornament, and multiple beaded necklaces (title "Himba-morsian" means "Himba bride" in Finnish), a clear documentary photo of Himba dress and adornment.

The image shows a beaded necklace with an oval iron/leather ornament, a traditional adornment type documented as Herero work; Himba and Herero are closely related neighbouring Namibian peoples whose material culture overlaps, so this plausibly belongs to the claimed ethnicity.
